For example, trackers may be imported under HTS code 8479.89.95.99 (“Electromechanical appliances with self-contained electric motor”) (U.S. International Trade Commission 2025e). However, this broad classification can include a wide range of other electromechanical devices used across various industries, such as manufacturing, agriculture, or industrial automation. In addition, companies may classify similar products under different HTS subcodes, depending on how their product descriptions align with the tariff schedule or based on interpretations by customs brokers, which further complicates efforts to track specific products. Overall, because tracker systems are assembled on-site from numerous components that are shipped to the project site, tracker imports and exports are best measured at the component level. 4.2.4 Regional Costs for Trackers Figure 49 shows tracker system prices in 2024. The modeled data, based on DOE benchmarks (U.S. Department of Energy 2024d), break down the national average U.S. tracker system price by component. The total U.S. modeled price is $0.14/W . Torque tubes account for 38% of the dc tracker price, followed by driven piles (20%), shipping (14%), and motors (10%). The other components constitute less than 10% of the system price each.
